title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: first — perseverance from God's gift (Jer. 32:40; 2 Thess. 3:3), not bare free choice
pass_a_gloss: I see nothing in this argument that can in any way be shaken or called into doubt. For first, if anyone should say that persevering faith can be foreseen in some to whom God has not yet decreed to give this perseverance, he would fetch so great a good from human choice, not from the Divine gift. But the whole Scripture protests, which shows the perseverance of the saints to flow from the gift of God: I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not depart from me, Jer. 32:40. 2 Thess. 3:3: Faithful is God, who will establish you and keep you from evil. And Augustine according to the Scriptures clearly taught that this possibility and will of persevering is given by the largess of Divine grace to the saints predestined into the kingdom of God, and not given to others. Therefore that of Aquinas is most true: The will of God by which he wills this good to someone in loving him is the cause that that good is had by him before others, Part 1, q. 23, art. 4.
pass_b_english: Nothing here can be shaken. First: if persevering faith could be foreseen in those to whom God has not yet decreed perseverance, that great good would come from human choice, not God's gift. All Scripture protests — saints' perseverance flows from God's gift: I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not depart from me (Jer. 32:40); Faithful is God, who will establish you and keep you from evil (2 Thess. 3:3). Augustine, following Scripture, taught that the power and will to persevere is given by grace's largess to saints predestined into God's kingdom — and not to others. So Aquinas is right: God's loving will that someone have this good is why he has it before others (ST 1.23.4).
source_text: Nihil video in hoc argumento quod ullo modo possit labefactari aut in dubium vocari. Nam primo, si quis diceret fidem perseverantem posse in aliquibus praevideri quibus Deus hanc perseverantiam nondum decreverit donare, ille tantum bonum ab humano arbitrio, non a Divino munere arcesseret. At tota Scriptura reclamat, quae perseverantiam sanctorum ex dono Dei ostendit dimanare: Reverentiam mei indam animo ipsorum, ut non recedant a me, Jer. xxxii. 40. 2 Thess. iii. 3. Fidelis est Deus, qui stabiliet vos et tuebitur a malo. Et Augustinus secundum Scripturas clare docuit, hanc perseverandi possibilitatem et voluntatem Divinae gratiae largitate donari sanctis in regnum Dei praedestinatis, aliis non donari. Est ergo verissimum illud Aquinatis: Voluntas Dei qua vult hoc bonum alicui diligendo, est causa quod illud bonum ab eo prae aliis habeatur, Part. 1. qu. 23. art. 4.
